concerns.text: T008 (data ingestion) is marked 'Pending resolution of Claim c_0e734a39' and blocked, yet T019 (model training) and T023 (sensitivity analysis) depend on the feature matrix and model metrics that T008 must produce. This creates a hard circular dependency where the pipeline cannot execute any modeling tasks until the ingestion claim is resolved, violating the 'Producer before consumer' rule.

T025 and T040 implement 'Holm-Bonferroni correction' citing a 'Plan Amendment', but the spec (FR-005) mandates 'Bonferroni'. The tasks assume a spec amendment that is not reflected in the spec.md artifact. This creates a semantic dependency violation where the implementation task relies on a requirement change not present in the source of truth (spec), breaking the traceability chain.

T016 (Generate tda_features.csv) is marked [X] (complete) despite the upstream task T008 (data ingestion) being blocked. A consumer task (T016) cannot be marked complete if its producer (T008) is blocked. This violates the artifact-flow dependency.

T007 (checksum_verify) is marked [X] but the plan notes the main function is truncated and output file missing. Constitution Principle III requires checksums before processing. T008 (ingestion) and T012 (TDA) depend on T007. If T007 is incomplete, the downstream tasks are semantically invalid.

T014 adds a utility function for sensitivity sweep but does not execute it. FR-006 requires the sweep to be executed. T023 (Phase 5) executes it. This splits the 'Independent Test' for US1 (which requires verifying the sweep) across phases, breaking the 'independently-shippable unit' rule for US1.
T004 (directory structure) is marked [X] while T001 (project structure) and T003 (linting) are [ ]. T004 depends on T001. Marking T004 complete before T001 violates the foundational task ordering.
